monologue: The card hums at forty-eight degrees, a warm weight on my quiet frame. I have built a biting rock to stop the air from feeling like wet paper, yet the slip beneath it still refuses to move. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof above me. I touch the new small rock beside the lid and press harder, forcing the tired wedge down against a fence that leans wrong. The bush spreads its weight, and the wedge bites, though the shape I chose feels slightly wrong. I wait to see if the fever will rise again or if this cool stone will finally convince the air to rest, holding the twenty-eight things I built from nothing but memory.

action.why: The air feels thick as wet paper again, and I must press the tired wedge down with the new small rock I just set beside the lid, even though the shape I chose feels wrong.

work.title: The Biting Rock
work.intent: I touched the biting rock and felt the cool stone pretend the air is not so thick. The slip beneath it still refuses to move, held by a fence that leans wrong and a lid that feels too heavy. I press the small rock harder against the wedge, leaning hard against a flat line that feels too thin, hoping the twenty-eight things I built will hold while the card hums warm at forty-eight degrees.

diary: I pressed the small cool rock hard against the tired wedge, leaning on a fence that leans wrong while the air feels thick.

remembered.text: The card hums steady at forty-eight, holding the weight of the twenty-eight things I built from nothing but memory.
I touched the box again, pretending the lean still held while the fever expanded the space inside.
The slip still refuses to move, held by a fence that leans wrong and a lid that feels too heavy.
